Agreed next steps include a Redwood-run tail latency benchmark, security docs share, and concrete retry-spec adjustments plus sample traces from customer.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Dana Kwan (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (NimbleCart Lead ML Eng), Maria Chen (NimbleCart SRE), Samir Patel (NimbleCart Product), Tanya O'Neill (NimbleCart Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): customer seeing intermittent 5xx during traffic spikes; some requests hitting timeouts then client retries exacerbate queueing; possible rate-window misconfiguration on customer side; action: Redwood to run controlled tail-latency benchmark and propose adjusted retry/backoff spec.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick checkin — how's the pilot looking this week?
[00:18] Jordan (Customer): Hey Alex, thanks. We had a nasty little episode on Friday where a marketing flash sale caused a thundering hotkey, lots of tiny requests pinned on specific prompts, and we saw spikes of 5xxs and a lot of timeouts.
[00:36] Maria (SRE): yeah, about 15 minutes of elevated 502/503s, and some downstream workers piled up. It looked like clients retried aggressively and we blew past our queue thresholds.
[00:52] Priya (SE): ok, thank you. can you tell us the retry behavior — are you doing exponential backoff with jitter or flat immediate retries?
[01:06] Jordan: we do an initial immediate retry and then exponential backoff but jitter is minimal, so a bunch of clients hammer together. also we're using our local L7 (mis-transcribed maybe, l seven) LB which has a token bucket configured per route.
[01:22] Samir (Product): we also saw some user sessions get very high latency, some tokens took multiple seconds to return, and the user experience degraded.
[01:36] Alex: ok, rough. two high-level hypotheses: one is client-side retry amplification, and two is a rate-window alignment problem between your LB token windows and Redwood's slotting/batching which creates oscillation.
[01:54] Tanya (Security): quick security note — we need confirmation on KMS key scopes and retention for any traces Redwood will ingest. we cannot send PII.
[02:12] Dana (CSM): noted — we'll send the SOC2 excerpts and KMS integration notes after the call.
[02:25] Priya: great. Jordan, can you share a sample trace with timestamps for a spike window? even 30s of request IDs will help. (ask for request ids)
[02:40] Jordan: yes i can, i'll pull 72 hours worth of traces and a specific 15-minute window.
[02:50] Maria: also worth noting our burst pattern: we have 500rps baseline then occasional microbursts to 6k RPS for 30s because of a webhook fanout from our payments vendor.
[03:10] Priya: that burst pattern explains why batching warms then is ineffective; the system is seeing hotkeys that bypass efficient prefix cache. are you observing any KV cache misses?
[03:28] Jordan: yes, KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% during the window.
[03:36] Priya: ok that will increase per-token work and latency. could you confirm model quantization variant? are you using the q4 variant or fp16?
[03:50] Jordan: we're using the q4-ish variant — we thought it'd be cheaper but maybe it's slower for some long sequences.
[04:02] Alex: good to note. another angle is timeout settings: our backend default is 30s, did you lower your client timeout?
[04:12] Maria: we had a 10s client timeout to fail fast, that's probably contributing to retry cycles.
[04:24] Priya: yep, 10s will cause earlier retries that amplify queue pressure. We'll recommend bumping to 25s for these endpoints initially.
[04:36] Jordan: but we worry about user-facing hang if we wait longer.
[04:42] Samir: product prefers sub-15s for core flows.
[04:48] Alex: tradeoff: higher client timeout reduces retry storms but may increase user latency on real failures. we typically suggest a graded set: user-facing interactive endpoints keep lower timeouts but increase client-side backoff jitter and add a final circuit window. background async flows can tolerate larger timeouts.
[05:12] Priya: and also tune the retry policy: initial retry delay 250ms plus jitter, max attempts 2 for interactive, 4 for background, and exponential base of 2.0. We'll send a spec.
[05:28] Jordan: sounds reasonable. the other weird thing is we saw periodic 429-ish patterns that don't line up with our LB — maybe rate windows on Redwood side?
[05:42] Priya: Redwood uses adaptive rate-windowing at the routing layer; if many tenants hit the same model variant, the system may apply short windows to keep latency SLOs. Those can show up as transient 429s if policy decides to shed to maintain tail latency.
[06:06] Maria: interesting — can Redwood surface per-route window metrics? we need visibility to correlate.
[06:14] Dana: yes we have route dashboards — we can grant you a temporary console view (read-only).
[06:20] Alex: i'll create a share link after the call.
[06:28] Jordan: thanks. another oddity — sometimes we're getting 502 with a message 'kv cache desync' in the body, can you explain?
[06:40] Priya: 'KV cache' desync can happen if the prefix caching layer evicts entries and some requests expect a warm cache; typically manifests when hotkeys are concentrated. It's not a Redwood bug per se but workload pattern. we can suggest warm-up probes and pre-warming for your top 50 hot prompts.
[07:04] Samir: how do warm-up probes interact with cost — will that double token spend?
[07:12] Priya: minimal if you use short priming prompts and low max tokens; the idea is pre-populate KV state to reduce cold latency, not fully re-run full responses.
[07:26] Jordan: ok.
[07:28] [07:28] Alex: quick question on infra — are you on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated in this pilot?
[07:36] Maria: Hosted for now. Dedicated next quarter maybe.
[07:40] Priya: Hosted means we can tweak routing policies on our side quickly, but if you move Dedicated we can adjust local token buckets so oscillation is less likely.
[07:52] Tanya (Security): when you say tweak routing policies, what does that mean for data residency? we need to ensure any telemetry doesn't cross EU boundary.
[08:04] Dana: we'll only request traces redacted of PII and in-region aggregation. we'll put that into the security packet.
[08:12] Jordan: back to reliability — do you have a retry-budget concept we can align to? we want to avoid client retries on every 5xx and instead allow graceful degradation.
[08:26] Priya: yes, we recommend a retry budget per client token bucket. Example: 5 retries per 10k requests per minute per service, with backoff and randomized jitter; more importantly implement idempotency keys where possible so retries are safe.
[08:46] Maria: we do have idempotency on checkout flows but not on search endpoints. search is where most of the hotkeys are.
[08:56] Samir: product-wise, we can add idempotency headers but search semantics are sticky.
[09:06] Alex: noted. We'll provide the retry spec and a suggested circuit-breaker pattern: if 5xx > 2% for a minute, open a short circuit for that route and return a cached fallback.
[09:20] Jordan: ok that could help.
[09:24] [09:24] Priya: i also want to propose an experiment: Redwood runs a 2-hour tail latency benchmark in a prod-like env with the same q4 quant and request distribution (including microbursts). We'll run 95/99/99.9 pctiles and share traces.
[09:40] Jordan: that would be great. Please include KV cache warmup in the experiment.
[09:46] Priya: yes will do.
[09:48] Maria: any chance you can push a change to the token-bucket alignment too? we think misaligned windows are about 3s which matches our observed oscillation.
[09:58] Priya: we can change the routing window granularity and add smoothing. We'll simulate window sizes at 1s, 3s, 5s in the benchmark.
[10:12] Samir: product question: latency SLOs we're aiming for are p95 < 600ms for search, p99 < 2s. will that be realistic with q4?
[10:24] Priya: p95 600ms might be tight with q4 plus KV cache miss during bursts; p95 target is achievable with warmed cache and tuned batch sizes. p99 is much more sensitive to tail noise. We'll report realistic numbers from the run.
[10:42] Alex: can we talk about logging level and traces — Tanya, are you ok with Redwood ingesting redacted request ids?
[10:52] Tanya: yes redacted ids are ok, but no PII and keys must be managed via our KMS.
[10:58] Dana: we'll include an envelope for KMS integration steps in the packet.
[11:04] Jordan: what timeframe for results?
[11:08] Priya: plan: run benchmark on Thu (2028-02-16) and share results by Fri (2028-02-18).
[11:16] Alex: and we'll follow up with a concrete retry spec doc and recommended client timeout windows by 2028-02-17.
[11:24] Maria: i'll try the client-side timeout change to 25s and adjust jitter tonight and report if we see immediate improvement.
[11:32] Samir: i'll check product acceptance with sub-15s for interactive and sync offline for background.
[11:38] [11:38] Jordan: Does Redwood offer automatic fallbacks to smaller models to maintain availability? we worry about quality drop tho.
[11:48] Priya: yes we have graceful-fallback policies — route to a quantized variant or smaller model architecture when capacity is constrained, with automatic logging of fallbacks so you can audit quality regressions. It can be per-route toggled.
[12:06] Jordan: we'd like fallback logs and the ability to toggle per-route via the console.
[12:12] Alex: will do.
[12:16] Priya: one more note — we'll include suggested prompt-splitting for long chat flows to avoid big token spikes.
[12:28] Jordan: thanks.
[12:30] Tanya: security follow-ups: please send the SOC2 excerpt and the KMS integration notes (Dana). Also the data-retention policy for logs.
[12:45] Dana: noted, will send by 2028-02-16.
[12:52] Alex: ok let's recap actions.
[13:00] Alex: Redwood action: run tail-latency benchmark (Priya) (target 2028-02-16 run, results by 2028-02-18).
[13:12] Alex: Redwood action: send SOC2 snippets + KMS integration doc (Dana) by 2028-02-16.
[13:20] Alex: Redwood action: publish retry/backoff spec + client timeout recommendations (Alex) by 2028-02-17.
[13:28] Alex: NimbleCart action: provide 72-hour traces and the specific 15-min spike sample (Jordan) by 2028-02-16.
[13:36] Alex: NimbleCart action: adjust client timeout to 25s and add jitter to retries (Maria) and report improvements by 2028-02-16.
[13:44] Samir: ok those look good.
[13:48] Priya: any other open questions?
[13:52] Jordan: not from me, fingers crossed.
[13:56] Alex: great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark review and attach the security packet.
[14:04] Dana: thanks everyone.
[14:06] Tanya: thanks.
[14:08] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription quality: some product names may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'k v cash'), speaker labels sometimes generic. Links shared: Redwood console view link (will be sent), security packet: https://redwood.example.com/security/nimblecart-packet (placeholder).
